shots.title: World below
shots.description: Proposed replacement for the last 52 frames of opening-005. Cut on To to a wide view: tiny ship at the upper-left, immense planet below. A modest widening settles before the next cut.
shots.transition: Cut from hands at the boundary to the world below; do not force a two-second trip through the shell.
shots.generationApproach: ImageGen wide starting frame from this geometry, then restrained Kling drift. A cut is safer than an ambitious shell-crossing reveal.

shots.title: The map opens outward
shots.description: Three-quarter interior medium shot. Harper summons a floating spatial diagram and spreads her fingers. The planet diagram reduces to an orbital system, then a local-star network. Continue across the musical gap to her reaction at frame 737.
shots.transition: Hard cut into the interior; fixed camera lets the map carry the movement. Cut to her reaction after the map settles.
shots.generationApproach: ImageGen establishes Harper, her hand pose and a faint diagram. Kling handles the performance; Blender supplies an independently composited planet/system/star expansion and stable invented glyphs. Keep diagram labels away from the lyric strip.

shots.title: Small cabin, enormous space
shots.description: Medium-close reaction: she glances from the map to the boundary, curiosity becoming restless longing. Let the diagram fade. Begin her gentle approach without a cut on The windows.
shots.transition: Start one continuous reaction-to-window take, shared with space-009. No new starting-frame reset at 789.

shots.title: Drawn to the boundary
shots.description: Continue the same take and screen direction. Harper floats toward the window, face and palms near the field but still inside. Keep one small metal-band cue so she reads as inside her ship, not outside it.
shots.transition: Continuation of space-008; this is a blocking beat, not an edit cut. Cut closer at frame 854.

shots.title: The cosmos in her eyes
shots.description: Close portrait at the boundary. Eyes dominate, with restrained reflected stars and a curved planet light. Hold a tiny breathing movement. Never turn the reflection into a second literal miniature planet beside her face.
shots.transition: Cut in at Show you just how big you are. End at Stretch your arms wide; no direction beyond that phrase has been assumed.
shots.generationApproach: ImageGen close portrait from the approved Harper reference, using Blender only for framing. Kling provides micro-expression; reflected cosmic light can be composited if generation makes it unstable.
